output.question: Why did EU support tickets spike in week 41?
output.summary: EU support tickets rose in week 41: The change is concentrated in the 'delivery_delay' and 'where_is_my_order' ticket categories: 39 tickets above the four-week mean, 100.0% of the total change [E2]. 41 of the 41 orders behind these tickets (100.0%) belong to carrier NordExpress, and 17 of those orders were cancelled [E4]. NordExpress shipments were late (three or more days) in 91.7% of cases in week 41 versus 11.9% in the four prior weeks [E5]

prior_knowledge.fact: Cancelled orders with reason 'delivery_delay' on carrier NordExpress rose from €159 in week 40 to €3,347 in week 41, a change of €3,188, while total net revenue dropped by only €3,007. Other segments moved the other way by €181, so this driver accounts for more than the whole change and its explained share is capped at 100.0%. NordExpress shipments were late (three or more days) in 91.7% of cases in week 41 versus 11.9% in the four prior weeks, and 37 of 42 affected orders had a late shipment. Support tickets rose to 52 in week 41 (four-week mean 14), and 50 of them (96.2%) are tied to NordExpress orders.
